name: Post-hoc diagnosis of E4.2 publication-scale failures
objective: Explain why CASPER_FULL loses Mission family-wise candidate coverage under S2/S3/S4 and why compute-health alarm coverage is low in S2/S4, without modifying or reinterpreting E4.2 outcomes.
diagnostic_questions: Are adaptive and health-enabled policies behaviorally distinguishable from RANKED_CP_STATIC at the run-level outcome metrics?
Does E1.7 eta actually depart from 1.0 under any E4.2 seed/scenario?
Does higher compute alarm coverage associate with improved late Mission FWC or DVR within S2/S4?
Are failures dominated by network-hidden degradation, compute-hidden degradation, or both?
Do aggregate data suffice to establish causality, or is task/node-level instrumentation required?
allowed_actions: add observational instrumentation only in a new E4.3 experiment if aggregate evidence is insufficient
forbidden_actions: change E4.2 workload, seeds, scenarios, deadlines, noise, calibration, policy parameters, health thresholds, probe budget, or CloudSim runtime
present post-hoc changes as if they were prelocked E4.2

initial_diagnostic_tests.policy_outcome_equivalence: exact/allclose comparison by seed and scenario across primary outcome metrics
initial_diagnostic_tests.adaptive_activation: distribution of late_eta for adaptive policies
initial_diagnostic_tests.health_association: within-scenario correlation of compute_alarm_coverage with late_fwc and late_dvr for CASPER_FULL
initial_diagnostic_tests.seed_gate_frequency: count seeds meeting late_fwc >= 0.99 by scenario

decision_rule: If aggregate diagnostics show inert or non-causal control layers but cannot identify the event-level mechanism, proceed to E4.3 trace-only instrumentation with the scientific decision rules frozen and no architecture tuning.
